task.title: Remove your two-factor authentication (2FA) requirement
task.shortdesc: You can remove the two-factor authentication for your Red Hat user account.

ul.li: Ensure you have a registered Red Hat user account with two-factor authentication enabled..
Ensure you have a smartphone or other device with the Google Authenticator app or the FreeOTP app installed.

prereq.note: You will be required to reenable two-factor authentication at your next login attempt if your Organization Administrator requires two-factor authentication for all users in the organization.
A new token is added to your authenticator app each time you disable and re-enable 2FA for your Red Hat account. It is your responsibility to manage disabled tokens on your device.

step.cmd: Log in to your Red Hat user account using two-factor authentication.

info.p: For instructions on signing in to your Red Hat user account using two-factor authentication, see
If you have lost your authenticator device and need Red Hat Support to revoke your two-factor authentication, see .

step.cmd: Click your user avatar in the upper right corner of the page.

substep.cmd: Click Account details. A page opens where you can edit your account information.
If you log in through Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, click My profile under your user avatar to edit your account information.

stepresult.p: A page opens where you can review your account information.
stepresult.note: Depending on which login portal you use, a different icon may appear.

step.cmd: On the Login & password page click Manage 2-factor authentication. The Signing in page opens.
Click Delete to remove two-factor authentication for your user login.

info.note: The Delete button disables, or turns off two-factor authentication for your user login. If you reenable two-factor authentication, you will repeat the enable authentication steps, which adds a new token to your authenticator app. The token associated with the disabled authenticator will no longer work.

step.cmd: For verification you must log in again with two-factor authentication. A page appears where you click CONFIRM DELETION to remove two-factor authentication from your user account. After you confirm deletion, you return to the Signing in page.
